open_obligations: Note that Sun et al.'s PRM rewards use human supervision on the easy tasks; check how this compares with Lightman et al.'s training data.
Check how model sizes compare between the two papers.
in.other_title: PRM rewards from easy-task supervision beat prior state-of-the-art trained on all levels
in.rationale: Lightman et al. evaluate reward models only by best-of-N and call RL on the generator a natural next step. Sun et al. compare PPO, DPO and ReST and report that models trained with PRM rewards, with human supervision on the easy tasks, reach a top performance of 34.0, outperforming the previous state of the art trained across all task levels (33.0), and that PRM rewards are more beneficial than final-answer rewards for hard tasks.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether process reward models remain useful when the generator is trained with RL against them
